newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BIL sees active Fairfax role.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BIL sees active Fairfax role.

text.p: Brierley Investments Ltd (BIL) said it would be an active investor in Australian newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.
It would also be interested in the Australian National Line (ANL) shipping group if it were put up for sales again, BIL chief executive Paul Collins said in a television interview screened on Sunday.

"I'd say in the case of Fairfax, we'll be a very active investor," Collins said after BIL's role in Fairfax was described by the interviewer as "really not much more than a passive investor", having bought into the group after some senior management changes.

"We'll be involved in this, as I think there are actually a number of very genuine revenue enhancing opportunities available inside the company which (Fairfax chief executive) Bob Muscat has identified," he said.
BIL acquired its 20 percent stake in Fairfax in December from Holoinger Group.
Collins also said BIL would be interest in looking at ANL if the government were to put it up for sale.

BIL already had other shipping interests in the region, such as Union Shipping and the Australia New Zealand Direct line, which made it one of the major players from the U.S. west coast down to Australia and New Zealand, Collins said.
"So clearly, if the government was going to look at selling ANL we would be interest in looking at that," he said.
The former Labor government had tried to sell ANL, but pulled out in late 1995 in the face of union pressure and decided to restructure the line for a later sale.

"But it depends very much on what the government offers for sale, the form it is at the time and I think that (if) it is offered by way of some form of public tender, we would certainly be interested in looking at that," Collins said.
